blocks.p: There's more to me than the Polyvagal Theory and mental health. I love doing this stuff, but there's more to me. I'm a dad. I have a daughter and a son. I usually like to teach, but this time I want to share a little story about my son, and the lesson he inadvertently bestowed upon me.

He loves being barefoot. The kid does not wear socks. Even if the house is cold and the floor is cold, he doesn't care. He doesn't even seem to notice. If you're a parent, tell me I'm not alone in this.

It's been raining here. We've had hardly a clear sky in what seems like at least a month. It's been rainy and cold and cloudy. So obviously that's sock weather, right? For anybody else, it is sock weather. But not for my wonderful son.

We had chores to do, so my wife and I both implored him to put on socks before we went out, but he declined. In fact, not only did he not wear socks, he slipped his little feet into sandals, and we just about died. I swear, as I think about it now, I'm just about dying again.

Wise parents pick their battles, and this one was not worth it. So we wished him good luck and headed out to do our errands. The natural consequence of chilly feet is probably more effective than artificial parent ones anyway. That was our thinking.

We'd been out for a while. We had finished our Target and Safeway stops, and then we got out of the car for our Sprouts stop. For some reason we do three or four shopping stops every weekend, I swear. And then we forget something and go back, or we make a midweek stop. And I say we, but really I make the midweek stop.
As we walked across the parking lot, I asked him how his feet were doing, because he was in sandals on a very cold day. Without missing a single beat, he said, "Great."
"Yeah," he said. "I love it. I can feel the air flowing between my toes. You should try it."
He recommended I try going sockless on a cold day, and I said, "I think I'll pass, son."
And he said to me in return, "It's really mindful, and I know you love mindfulness."
I think he said it in kind of a snide manner, for sure. But he was serious too, and I don't think he was wrong. That's the thing. I don't think he was wrong.

blocks.why: This article talks about mindfulness. This practice gives you a few minutes of it.

blocks.p: So what did I learn? A few things.

I learned that he knows what he needs, and he can make informed decisions. Of course, my wife and I will keep making sure he's headed in the right general direction in life, but he can decide on socks or not, it would seem.

Another thing: mindfulness shows up differently for everybody. I won't go sockless in the cold anytime soon, but I'm glad he can mindfully connect with that experience. He did the same thing again, actually, with shoes instead of sandals. It's obviously not a battle worth picking, and he likes it. So whatever.

I can actually relate to his socklessness in my own way. Every morning I open the bathroom window when I shower. It lets in the cold morning air, and it just kind of feels right. I love looking out the window at the oranges and grapefruits growing in the backyard, and I like feeling the air's chill in contrast to the heat of the water.
So, to wrap it up: I don't know if this is relevant to your life, but can you relate in some way? Do you have your own sockless mindfulness practice?
